source.subject: mathematics
source.notes: Paper prints: Series 1PQRS, SET-1, Q.P. Code 65/1/1, 23 printed pages (+1 cover), 38 questions, Maximum Marks 80, Time allowed 3 hours. Session is not printed on the paper. English text is on odd PDF pages (Hindi on even pages, page 1 is a bilingual cover). This is a Mathematics paper: the PDF's text layer systematically drops many mathematical glyphs that other CBSE papers keep as plain text, specifically ≤, ≥, ∈, ×, ·, ∩, π, √, ∫, the transpose prime ('), the vector-line parameter λ and vector arrow/hat marks, while <, >, +, -, =, digits, letters and | (absolute value) extract normally; multi-row matrices/determinants collapse to flattened digit strings. Per the brief, such losses were left as extracted and flagged with 'Mathematical notation lost in extraction' at LOW confidence rather than guessed; only unambiguous stacked fractions and plain integer powers (e.g. 'x2' -> 'x²') were rebuilt, at MEDIUM confidence. The official marking scheme's Section A (Q1-20, MCQ and Assertion-Reason) shows the correct option only as an image/highlight with no extractable text at all for any of the 20 items, so officialAnswer is omitted for Q1-20 and flagged instead. The marking scheme's Section B-E extracts with much better Unicode math (√, ∫, italic variables) and was used, trimmed to final value points; a few multi-step workings and one diagram (Q38(i)) are images and were flagged as lost working rather than reproduced. The rupee sign extracted as a backtick '`' in the case-study questions and was normalised to ₹ (unambiguous one-to-one substitution).

questions.text: A relation R is defined on Z, the set of integers, as R = {(x, y) : |x – y| is divisible by a prime number 'p', x, y Z} check whether R is an equivalence relation or not.
extractionIssues: Mathematical notation lost in extraction (∈ symbol before 'Z' in the relation's definition); see page 17

officialAnswer.text: R is reflexive (|x–x|=0, divisible by any prime), symmetric (|x–y|=|y–x|), and transitive (if p|(x–y) and p|(y–z) then p|(x–z)); hence R is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: A function f : R – {3/5} → R – {3/5} is defined as f(x) = (3x + 2)/(5x – 3). Show that f is one-one and onto.

officialAnswer.text: One-one: f(x1)=f(x2) ⇒ x1=x2. Onto: for y∈R–{3/5}, x=(3y+2)/(5y–3)∈ domain satisfies f(x)=y. Hence f is one-one and onto.

questions.text:
An online delivery company in a city has 5000 subscribers and collects annual subscription fees of ₹300 per subscriber for unlimited free deliveries.
The company wishes to increase the annual subscription fee. It is predicted that, for every increase of ₹1, ten subscribers will discontinue. Assume that the company increased the annual fee by ₹x.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions :
(i) How many subscribers will discontinue after an increase of ₹x in annual fee ? (1)
(ii) If R(x) denotes the total revenue collected after the increase of ₹x in subscription fee, express R(x) as a function of x. (1)
(iii) (a) Find the value of x for which R(x) is maximum. (2)
OR
(iii) (b) Find the sub-intervals of (0, 5000) in which R(x) is increasing and decreasing. (2)
extractionIssues: Sub-part marks shown in brackets were printed in the margin

officialAnswer.text:
(i) 10x
(ii) R(x) = (5000 – 10x)(300 + x)
(iii)(a) R′(x) = 2000 – 20x; R′(x)=0 ⇒ x=100; R″(x)=–20<0, so R(x) is maximum at x=100
OR
(iii)(b) R(x) is increasing in (0,100) and decreasing in (100,5000)

In an online jackpot, there is one first prize of ₹3,00,000, two second prizes of ₹2,00,000 each and three third prizes of ₹50,000 each.
A total of 1,00,000 jackpot tickets each costing ₹100 were sold there by raising a fund of ₹1,00,00,000.
Rohan bought one ticket.
Based on given information, answer the following questions :
(i) What are the possible amounts, the person can win ? (1)
(ii) (a) What is the probability that the person wins atleast ₹2,00,000 ? (2)
OR
(ii) (b) What is the probability that the person does not win any amount ? (2)
(iii) In another jackpot, Rohan also bought a ticket having a prize money of ₹5,00,000. The chances of winning the jackpot are 1 in 1,00,000. Find the probability that on exactly one of tickets he wins the jackpot. (1)

Roundabouts are often made on busy roads to ease the traffic and avoid red lights.
One such round-about is made such that equation representing its boundary is given by C1 : x² + y² = 64.
There is a circular pond with a fountain in the middle of the roundabout whose equation is given by C2 : x² + y² = 4.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions :
(i) Represent the given equations C1 and C2 with the help of a diagram. (1)
(ii) Express y as a function of x, (y = f(x)), for both C1 and C2. (1)
(iii) (a) Using integration find the area of region covered by the roundabout. (2)
OR
(iii) (b) Using integration, find the area of region covered by circular pond. (2)
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (powers x², y²); check against the PDF
Official answer for (i) is a diagram image not in the text layer

officialAnswer.text:
(ii) C1: y=√(64–x²) or y=–√(64–x²); C2: y=√(4–x²) or y=–√(4–x²)
(iii)(a) Area = 4∫₀⁸√(64–x²)dx = 64π
OR
(iii)(b) Area = 4∫₀²√(4–x²)dx = 4π
